**Punta Maroma Combined GAM**

25. This and the next three code blocks (26-28) define tailored procedures to evaluate the best‑performing GAM for each site using both training fit statistics and cross‑validation. The function first identifies the optimal model from the parsimony table (`pars_table`) based on minimum AIC, retrieves the corresponding formula, and fits a beta regression GAM with logit link. Model diagnostics are extracted, including AIC, mean squared error (MSE), adjusted R2, and deviance explained. A five‑fold cross‑validation is then performed, with the dataset partitioned into folds, models refitted on training subsets, and predictions generated for held‑out data. Fold‑specific metrics (deviance explained and MSE) are aggregated, and summary statistics (mean, range, and standard deviation) are computed. Results are organized into two outputs: (i) a performance table (`Performance`) reporting overall fit and cross‑validation metrics, and (ii) a predictor table (`Predictors`) listing smooth and linear terms, effective degrees of freedom, test statistics, p‑values, and significance codes. These functions thus provide a comprehensive evaluation of the selected GAM, combining parsimony, fit quality, and predictive reliability for each site-panel.

```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(caret)
run_gam_cv_pm <- function(datos_pm, formulas_cb, pars_table) {
  best_model <- pars_table %>%
    filter(Segment == "Punta Maroma") %>%
    slice_min(AIC, n = 1) %>%
    pull(Model)

  formula <- formulas_cb[[best_model]]
  n_smooth <- count_smooth_terms(formula)
  k_max <- safe_k_for(nrow(datos_pm), n_smooth)
  formula <- if (n_smooth > 0) cap_smooth_k(formula, k_max) else formula

mod <- bam(formula,
             data = datos_pm,
             family = betar(link = "logit"),
             method = "fREML",
             select = TRUE,
             discrete = TRUE)

  smry <- summary(mod)
  aic_val <- AIC(mod)
  mse_train <- mean(residuals(mod)^2)
  r2_train <- smry$r.sq
  dev_train <- smry$dev.expl

set.seed(7341)
  folds <- createFolds(datos_pm$counts_norm_sv, k = 5)
  cv_list <- lapply(seq_along(folds), function(i) {
    test_idx <- folds[[i]]
    train <- datos_pm[-test_idx, ]
    test <- datos_pm[test_idx, ]
    mod_cv <- bam(formula, data = train,
                  family = betar(link = "logit"),
                  method = "fREML",
                  select = TRUE,
                  discrete = TRUE)
    preds <- predict(mod_cv, newdata = test, type = "response")
    ss_res <- sum((test$counts_norm_sv - preds)^2)
    ss_tot <- sum((test$counts_norm_sv - mean(test$counts_norm_sv))^2)
    dev <- 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
    mse_cv <- mean((test$counts_norm_sv - preds)^2)
    data.frame(fold = i, dev_expl = dev, mse = mse_cv)
  })
  cv_results <- do.call(rbind, cv_list)

  dev_mean <- mean(cv_results$dev_expl)
  dev_range <- paste0(round(min(cv_results$dev_expl), 2), "–", round(max(cv_results$dev_expl), 2))
  mse_mean <- mean(cv_results$mse)
  mse_sd <- sd(cv_results$mse)

 perf <- tibble(
    Site = "Punta Maroma",
    Model = best_model,
    AIC = round(aic_val, 2),
    Explained_Deviance = round(dev_train * 100, 1),
    `Explained_Deviance_(5fold)` = paste0(round(dev_mean, 2), " (", dev_range, ")"),
    `MSE_±SD` = paste0(round(mse_mean, 3), " ± ", round(mse_sd, 3)),
    R2_Adj = round(r2_train, 3)
  )

  smooths <- as.data.frame(smry$s.table)
  smooths$Term <- rownames(smry$s.table)
  stat_col <- intersect(c("Chi.sq", "F", "Statistic"), colnames(smooths))
  smooths$Stat <- if (length(stat_col) == 0) NA else smooths[[stat_col[1]]]
  smooths <- smooths %>%
    mutate(Type = "Smooth",
           Significance = case_when(
             `p-value` < 0.001 ~ "***",
             `p-value` < 0.01 ~ "**",
             `p-value` < 0.05 ~ "*",
             `p-value` < 0.1 ~ ".",
             TRUE ~ "ns"
           )) %>%
    select(Term, edf = `edf`, Stat, p_value = `p-value`, Significance, Type)

  linears <- as.data.frame(smry$p.table)
  linears$Term <- rownames(smry$p.table)
  # The parametric-term p-value column is named "Pr(>|t|)" or "Pr(>|z|)"
  # depending on the estimation method/family combination (this varies,
  # e.g., between bam() and gam() fits) - detect whichever is present
  # instead of hardcoding one, to avoid failures like the one this caused
  # for Saint Croix's gam()-fitted model.
  pcol <- intersect(c("Pr(>|t|)", "Pr(>|z|)"), colnames(linears))[1]
  linears <- linears %>%
    mutate(Type = "Linear",
           edf = NA,
           Stat = NA,
           p_value_tmp = .data[[pcol]],
           Significance = case_when(
             p_value_tmp < 0.001 ~ "***",
             p_value_tmp < 0.01 ~ "**",
             p_value_tmp < 0.05 ~ "*",
             p_value_tmp < 0.1 ~ ".",
             TRUE ~ "ns"
           )) %>%
    select(Term, edf, Stat, p_value = p_value_tmp, Significance, Type)

  predictors <- bind_rows(smooths, linears)

  pred <- tibble(
    Site = "Punta Maroma",
    Model = best_model,
    Predictor = predictors$Term,
    EDF = round(predictors$edf, 2),
    Chi_sq = round(predictors$Stat, 2),
    p_value = format(predictors$p_value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
    Significance = predictors$Significance,
    Type = predictors$Type
  )

  list(Performance = perf, Predictors = pred)
}

results_pm <- run_gam_cv_pm(datos_pm, formulas_cb, pars_table)

results_pm$Performance
results_pm$Predictors

```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
run_gam_cv_fl <- function(datos_fl, formulas_cb, pars_table) {
  best_model <- pars_table %>%
    filter(Segment == "Florida") %>%

  formula <- formulas_cb[[best_model]]

  formula <- if (n_smooth > 0) cap_smooth_k(formula, k_max) else formula
  
  mod <- bam(formula,
             data = datos_fl,
             family = betar(link = "logit"),
             method = "fREML",
             select = TRUE,
             discrete = TRUE)
  
  smry <- summary(mod)
  aic_val <- AIC(mod)
  mse_train <- mean(residuals(mod)^2)
  r2_train <- smry$r.sq
  dev_train <- smry$dev.expl
  
  # Cross validation 5‑fold
  set.seed(7341)
  folds <- createFolds(datos_fl$counts_norm_sv, k = 5)
  cv_list <- lapply(seq_along(folds), function(i) {
    test_idx <- folds[[i]]

    test <- datos_fl[test_idx, ]
    mod_cv <- bam(formula, data = train,
                  family = betar(link = "logit"),

                  select = TRUE,
                  discrete = TRUE)
    preds <- predict(mod_cv, newdata = test, type = "response")
    ss_res <- sum((test$counts_norm_sv - preds)^2)
    ss_tot <- sum((test$counts_norm_sv - mean(test$counts_norm_sv))^2)
    dev <- 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
    mse_cv <- mean((test$counts_norm_sv - preds)^2)
    data.frame(fold = i, dev_expl = dev, mse = mse_cv)
  })
  cv_results <- do.call(rbind, cv_list)
  
  dev_mean <- mean(cv_results$dev_expl)
  dev_range <- paste0(round(min(cv_results$dev_expl), 2), "–", round(max(cv_results$dev_expl), 2))
  mse_mean <- mean(cv_results$mse)
  mse_sd <- sd(cv_results$mse)
  
  perf <- tibble(
    Site = "Florida",
    Model = best_model,
    AIC = round(aic_val, 2),
    Explained_Deviance = round(dev_train * 100, 1),
    `Explained_Deviance_(5fold)` = paste0(round(dev_mean, 2), " (", dev_range, ")"),
    `MSE_±SD` = paste0(round(mse_mean, 3), " ± ", round(mse_sd, 3)),
    R2_Adj = round(r2_train, 3)
  )
 
  smooths <- as.data.frame(smry$s.table)
  smooths$Term <- rownames(smry$s.table)
  stat_col <- intersect(c("Chi.sq", "F", "Statistic"), colnames(smooths))
  smooths$Stat <- if (length(stat_col) == 0) NA else smooths[[stat_col[1]]]
  smooths <- smooths %>%
    mutate(Type = "Smooth",
           Significance = case_when(
             `p-value` < 0.001 ~ "***",
             `p-value` < 0.01 ~ "**",
             `p-value` < 0.05 ~ "*",
             `p-value` < 0.1 ~ ".",
             TRUE ~ "ns"
           )) %>%
    select(Term, edf = `edf`, Stat, p_value = `p-value`, Significance, Type)
  
  linears <- as.data.frame(smry$p.table)
  linears$Term <- rownames(smry$p.table)
  # The parametric-term p-value column is named "Pr(>|t|)" or "Pr(>|z|)"
  # depending on the estimation method/family combination (this varies,
  # e.g., between bam() and gam() fits) - detect whichever is present
  # instead of hardcoding one, to avoid failures like the one this caused
  # for Saint Croix's gam()-fitted model.
  pcol <- intersect(c("Pr(>|t|)", "Pr(>|z|)"), colnames(linears))[1]
  linears <- linears %>%
    mutate(Type = "Linear",
           edf = NA,
           Stat = NA,
           p_value_tmp = .data[[pcol]],
           Significance = case_when(
             p_value_tmp < 0.001 ~ "***",
             p_value_tmp < 0.01 ~ "**",
             p_value_tmp < 0.05 ~ "*",
             p_value_tmp < 0.1 ~ ".",
             TRUE ~ "ns"
           )) %>%
    select(Term, edf, Stat, p_value = p_value_tmp, Significance, Type)
  
  predictors <- bind_rows(smooths, linears)
  
  pred <- tibble(
    Site = "Florida",
    Model = best_model,
    Predictor = predictors$Term,
    EDF = round(predictors$edf, 4),
    Chi_sq = round(predictors$Stat, 4),
    p_value = format(predictors$p_value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
    Significance = predictors$Significance,
    Type = predictors$Type
  )
  
  list(Performance = perf, Predictors = pred)
}
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
run_gam_cv_bz <- function(datos_bz, formulas_cb, pars_table) {
 
  best_model <- pars_table %>%
    filter(Segment == "Belize") %>%
    slice_min(deltaAIC, n = 1) %>%
    pull(Model)
  
  formula <- formulas_cb[[best_model]]
  n_smooth <- count_smooth_terms(formula)
  k_max <- safe_k_for(nrow(datos_bz), n_smooth)
  formula <- if (n_smooth > 0) cap_smooth_k(formula, k_max) else formula
  
  mod <- bam(formula,
             data = datos_bz,
             family = betar(link = "logit"),
             method = "fREML",
             select = TRUE,
             discrete = TRUE)
  
  smry <- summary(mod)
  aic_val <- AIC(mod)
  mse_train <- mean(residuals(mod)^2)
  r2_train <- smry$r.sq
  dev_train <- smry$dev.expl
  
  set.seed(7341)
  folds <- createFolds(datos_bz$counts_norm_sv, k = 5)
  cv_list <- lapply(seq_along(folds), function(i) {
    test_idx <- folds[[i]]
    train <- datos_bz[-test_idx, ]
    test <- datos_bz[test_idx, ]
    mod_cv <- bam(formula, data = train,
                  family = betar(link = "logit"),
                  method = "fREML",
                  select = TRUE,
                  discrete = TRUE)
    preds <- predict(mod_cv, newdata = test, type = "response")
    ss_res <- sum((test$counts_norm_sv - preds)^2)
    ss_tot <- sum((test$counts_norm_sv - mean(test$counts_norm_sv))^2)
    dev <- 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
    mse_cv <- mean((test$counts_norm_sv - preds)^2)
    data.frame(fold = i, dev_expl = dev, mse = mse_cv)
  })
  cv_results <- do.call(rbind, cv_list)
  
  dev_mean <- mean(cv_results$dev_expl)
  dev_range <- paste0(round(min(cv_results$dev_expl), 2), "–", round(max(cv_results$dev_expl), 2))
  mse_mean <- mean(cv_results$mse)
  mse_sd <- sd(cv_results$mse)
  
  perf <- tibble(
    Site = "Belize",
    Model = best_model,
    AIC = round(aic_val, 2),
    Explained_Deviance = round(dev_train * 100, 1),
    `Explained_Deviance_(5fold)` = paste0(round(dev_mean, 2), " (", dev_range, ")"),
    `MSE_±SD` = paste0(round(mse_mean, 3), " ± ", round(mse_sd, 3)),
    R2_Adj = round(r2_train, 3)
  )
  
  smooths <- as.data.frame(smry$s.table)
  smooths$Term <- rownames(smry$s.table)
  stat_col <- intersect(c("Chi.sq", "F", "Statistic"), colnames(smooths))
  smooths$Stat <- if (length(stat_col) == 0) NA else smooths[[stat_col[1]]]
  smooths <- smooths %>%
    mutate(Type = "Smooth",
           Significance = case_when(
             `p-value` < 0.001 ~ "***",
             `p-value` < 0.01 ~ "**",
             `p-value` < 0.05 ~ "*",
             `p-value` < 0.1 ~ ".",
             TRUE ~ "ns"
           )) %>%
    select(Term, edf = `edf`, Stat, p_value = `p-value`, Significance, Type)
  
  linears <- as.data.frame(smry$p.table)
  linears$Term <- rownames(smry$p.table)
  # The parametric-term p-value column is named "Pr(>|t|)" or "Pr(>|z|)"
  # depending on the estimation method/family combination (this varies,
  # e.g., between bam() and gam() fits) - detect whichever is present
  # instead of hardcoding one, to avoid failures like the one this caused
  # for Saint Croix's gam()-fitted model.
  pcol <- intersect(c("Pr(>|t|)", "Pr(>|z|)"), colnames(linears))[1]
  linears <- linears %>%
    mutate(Type = "Linear",
           edf = NA,
           Stat = NA,
           p_value_tmp = .data[[pcol]],
           Significance = case_when(
             p_value_tmp < 0.001 ~ "***",
             p_value_tmp < 0.01 ~ "**",
             p_value_tmp < 0.05 ~ "*",
             p_value_tmp < 0.1 ~ ".",
             TRUE ~ "ns"
           )) %>%
    select(Term, edf, Stat, p_value = p_value_tmp, Significance, Type)
  
  predictors <- bind_rows(smooths, linears)
  
  pred <- tibble(
    Site = "Belize",
    Model = best_model,
    Predictor = predictors$Term,
    EDF = round(predictors$edf, 2),
    Chi_sq = round(predictors$Stat, 2),
    p_value = format(predictors$p_value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3),
    Significance = predictors$Significance,
    Type = predictors$Type
  )
  
  list(Performance = perf, Predictors = pred)
}
```

**Suppl.Table 4. Five‑fold cross‑validation performance across reef sites an regional scope.** Reported metrics include AIC, deviance explained, adjusted R², mean squared error (MSE ± SD), and cross‑validated deviance explained. Results show strong in‑sample fits but limited predictive stability, with predominantly negative or near‑zero values across folds.

**Suppl.Table 5. Predictor‑level summary statistics from best fitted combined GAMs across reef sites an regional scope** showing individual smooth and linear terms along with their effective degrees of feedom (EDF), test statistic (ch-square for smooths) and *p*-value, For linear terms, *p*-value corresponds to *Pr(\>\|t\|).*

Cross validation stability in both marginal and combined models is strongly constrained by data quality. Marginal models achieved occasional consistency across sites, while combined models only sustained modest but positive generalization in the Regional panel. Since the primary aim of this study was reconstructive rather than predictive, the viability and reliability of the modeling were assessed primarily through parameters such as effective degrees of freedom (EDF), Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), and residual diagnostics—metrics that are standard in ecological reconstruction studies. The next section therefore opens the validation through model-based metrics, highlighting how these indicators support the paleoecological interpretation despite the limitations revealed by cross-validation.

### 4.4 GAM checking procedure

To ensure methodological transparency and meet standard practices in GAM-based ecological modeling, we include diagnostic plots of residual behavior in this Supplementary Material. These visual procedures allow us to complement the quantitative metrics (adjusted R², MSE, EDF, k-index), and to confirm that the model does not exhibit systematic bias or structural misfit. We report the diagnostic suite generated by *gam.check()*.

### 4.4.1 gam.check and plot.gam

The *gam.check()* visual outcome in the **Suppl. Fig. 6** provides a more comprehensive evaluation, including a Q-Q plot to assess normality, a histogram of residuals, residuals versus the linear predictor, and observed versus fitted values for each selected best GAM fitted.  

**Suppl. Material 2. Diagnostic plots for the fitted GAM model, via *gam.check()*** Compilation includes Q-Q plot, histogram of residuals, residuals vs. linear predictor, and response vs. fitted values for each reef site and the regional scope.

**4.4.3 Combined GAM Visual Outcome**

29. This chunk thus provides a comparative visualization of the fitted GAMs, illustrating how climatic and disturbance predictors shape coral fossil density across local and regional scales for each site (***Punta Maroma*****, *Florida*, *Belize***) and the **regional** aggregate, using beta regression with logit link and restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Summaries of each fitted model are generated to evaluate explanatory power and significance of predictors. A consistent color scheme is defined for sites, and all models are collected into a list for streamlined processing. Smooth estimates and confidence intervals are extracted with the `gratia` package, pooled across sites, and reshaped into a long format for visualization. The resulting plot (`p_all`) displays partial effects of predictors (age, temperature anomalies, rates of change, hurricane frequency and averages) with smooth curves and shaded confidence ribbons, faceted by predictor to highlight variable‑specific responses. Colors and fills distinguish sites, while minimalist formatting emphasizes interpretability. The figure output corresponds to the main text' **Figure 4**. **Generalized Additive Model (GAM) partial effect plots** which here is exported as a high‑resolution PDF for publication.

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}

library(gratia)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Fit each site's best combined GAM *dynamically* from the model actually
# selected by the parsimony analysis (`pars_table`), instead of hardcoding
# formulas here (previously this chunk used the wrong hurricane-metric
# branch for Belize, and an ad hoc marginal formula for Saint Croix that
# had never gone through the selection process). Basis dimension is capped
# via `cap_smooth_k()`/`safe_k_for()` for safety on small panels.
fit_selected_best <- function(site, data, pars_table, formulas_cb) {
  best_model <- pars_table %>%
    filter(Segment == site) %>%
    slice_min(AIC, n = 1) %>%
    pull(Model)

  f <- formulas_cb[[best_model]]
  n_smooth <- count_smooth_terms(f)
  k_max <- safe_k_for(nrow(data), n_smooth)
  f_safe <- if (n_smooth > 0) cap_smooth_k(f, k_max) else f

  if (nrow(data) > 100) {
    bam(f_safe, data = data, family = betar(link = "logit"),
        method = "fREML", select = TRUE, discrete = TRUE)
  } else {
    gam(f_safe, data = data, family = betar(link = "logit"),
        method = "REML", select = TRUE)
  }
}

best_model_pm  <- fit_selected_best("Punta Maroma", datos_pm,  pars_table, formulas_cb)
best_model_fl  <- fit_selected_best("Florida",      datos_fl,  pars_table, formulas_cb)
best_model_bz  <- fit_selected_best("Belize",       datos_bz,  pars_table, formulas_cb)
best_model_sc  <- fit_selected_best("Saint Croix",  datos_sc,  pars_table, formulas_cb)
best_model_reg <- fit_selected_best("Regional",     datos_reg, pars_table, formulas_cb)

summary(best_model_pm)
summary(best_model_fl)
summary(best_model_bz)
summary(best_model_sc)
summary(best_model_reg)

custom_colors <- c(
  "Punta Maroma" = "#D55E00",
  "Florida"      = "#0072B2",
  "Saint Croix"  = "#F0E442",
  "Belize"       = "#CCBB44",
  "Regional"     = "#332288"
)

best_models <- list(
  "Punta Maroma" = best_model_pm,
  "Florida"      = best_model_fl,
  "Belize"       = best_model_bz,
  "Saint Croix"  = best_model_sc,
   "Regional"     = best_model_reg
)

df_all <- purrr::map_df(names(best_models), function(site) {
  smooth_estimates(best_models[[site]], ci_level = 0.95) %>%
    add_confint() %>%
    mutate(site = site)
})

df_all <- df_all %>%
  mutate(site = factor(site, levels = names(custom_colors)))

smooth_predictor_cols <- intersect(
  c("age", "GMHT_CPS0_30N", "dT_raw", "Hur100_av", "Hur100_fqcy"),
  names(df_all)
)

df_long <- df_all %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(smooth_predictor_cols),
               names_to = "predictor", values_to = "xvar") %>%
  filter(!is.na(xvar))

p_all <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = xvar, y = .estimate, colour = site, fill = site)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower_ci, ymax = .upper_ci), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
  facet_wrap(~predictor, scales = "free") +   # <- eje X y Y libres
  scale_colour_manual(values = custom_colors, breaks = names(custom_colors)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors, breaks = names(custom_colors)) +
  labs(y = "Partial effect", x = "Predictor") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text  = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
p_all 
 ggsave("Figure_3.pdf", plot = p_all, width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300, device = cairo_pdf)
```

Next four code blocks ( 30- 33) perform diagnostic checks and visualizations for each best GAM fitted to the *site-specific* datasets. The `gam.check` function is used to assess model adequacy, producing standard diagnostic plots (residuals vs. fitted values, Q–Q plot, histogram of residuals, and residuals vs. linear predictor). These are arranged in a 2×2 grid for clarity. Subsequently, partial effect plots for all smooth terms are generated with `plot`, using shaded confidence intervals and rug plots to indicate data density along the predictor axes. The layout is set to a 2×3 grid, allowing simultaneous inspection of multiple predictors. Together, these diagnostics provide a comprehensive evaluation of model fit, residual behavior, and the functional form of predictor effects, ensuring both statistical validity and ecological interpretability of the GAM results for *each site*.

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
par(mfrow = c(2,3))
plot(best_models[["Punta Maroma"]], shade=TRUE, pages=1, all.terms=TRUE, rug=TRUE)
```

### 4.5 Residuals' Temporal Independency Analysis

The residual independency analysis underscores clear site‑specific differences in temporal autocorrelation. While **Punta Maroma** and **Regional** models achieve residual independence, **Belize** demonstrates acceptable independence, whereas **Florida** retains moderate autocorrelation. These diagnostics confirm that temporal dependence is site‑specific, with Florida emerging as the most problematic case.

At **Punta Maroma** (M4_av), residuals show slight negative autocorrelation (φ_AR1 = −0.31, DW = 2.50, p = 0.91; Ljung–Box p = 0.63), indicating overall independence and confirming that the model captures local dynamics without leaving temporal dependence. The **Regional** model (M7_av) also achieves residual independence, with slightly negative autocorrelation (φ_AR1 = −0.22, DW = 2.39, p = 0.81; Ljung–Box p = 0.46), suggesting that aggregated signals, despite diluting site‑specific variability, retain a stable temporal structure. Hence, these two models can be interpreted with confidence.

For **Belize** (M6_fqcy), residuals are close to independence (φ_AR1 = 0.06, DW = 1.83, p = 0.31; Ljung–Box p = 0.70), showing no significant evidence of autocorrelation and suggesting acceptable stability. This site‑specific model provides useful, though somewhat less robust, inference.

In contrast, **Florida** (M7_av) exhibits moderate positive autocorrelation (φ_AR1 = 0.27, DW = 1.44, p = 0.027; Ljung–Box p = 0.11), consistent with short‑term dependence and weaker temporal fit. This residual pattern requires caution: additional model refinement (e.g., incorporating correlation structures or alternative predictors) may be necessary to avoid biased inference.

**Suppl.Table 7. Residual independency analysis across fitted combined model across reef sites and the regional scope.** Reported metrics include lag‑1 autocorrelation (φ_AR1), Durbin–Watson statistics and p‑values, and Ljung–Box test results. Findings highlight strong autocorrelation in Belize and Regional models, moderate dependence in Florida and Saint Croix, and near‑independent residuals in Punta Maroma.

34. This code block evaluates the temporal independence of residuals from the best GAMs across all sites (***Belize*****, *Florida*, *Punta Maroma*, *Regional*, *Saint Croix***). A helper function (`check_temporal_independence`) computes diagnostic statistics: the AR(1) coefficient (ϕ), the Durbin–Watson statistic and p‑value, and the Ljung–Box test statistic and p‑value, using Pearson residuals. For each site, the best model (selected by minimum AIC) is refitted, residuals are extracted, and diagnostics are compiled into a summary table. Autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions (ACF/PACF) are plotted for each site, saved as a PDF for publication. Additional helper functions (`acf_df`, `pacf_df`) convert ACF/PACF outputs into tidy data frames, which are combined across sites. A comparative visualization (`plot_acf_pacf`) is then generated, showing bar plots of ACF and PACF values by lag, faceted by site and diagnostic type, with dashed lines indicating approximate confidence bounds. This routine provides a systematic assessment of residual independence, ensuring that temporal autocorrelation does not bias inference and highlighting differences in residual structure across reef sites and the regional aggregate.

```{r,echo=FALSE}

data_list <- list(
  "Belize"       = datos_bz,
  "Florida"      = datos_fl,
  "Punta Maroma" = datos_pm,
  "Regional"     = datos_reg,
  "Saint Croix"  = datos_sc
)

library(mgcv)
library(lmtest)

check_temporal_independence <- function(mod) {
  # Extraer residuales tipo pearson
  res_raw <- residuals(mod, type = "pearson")
  if (is.list(res_raw)) res_raw <- unlist(res_raw)
  res_raw <- as.numeric(res_raw)
  
  # AR(1) coeficiente
  phi <- cor(res_raw[-1], res_raw[-length(res_raw)])
  
  # Durbin–Watson
  dw <- lmtest::dwtest(res_raw ~ 1)
  
  # Ljung–Box
  lb <- Box.test(res_raw, lag = 10, type = "Ljung-Box")
  
  list(
    phi_AR1 = phi,
    DW_stat = dw$statistic,
    DW_pval = dw$p.value,
    LB_stat = lb$statistic,
    LB_pval = lb$p.value,
    res_raw = res_raw
  )
}

## Note: named `best_models_table` (rather than `best_models`) to avoid
## shadowing the `best_models` list of *fitted* model objects created in
## the previous chunk (used there by gam.check()/plot()).
best_models_table <- pars_table %>%
  group_by(Segment) %>%
  slice_min(AIC, n = 1) %>%
  select(Segment, Model)

results_resid <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(best_models_table)), function(i) {
  seg <- best_models_table$Segment[i]
  mname <- best_models_table$Model[i]
  cat("Adjusting model:", mname, "for segment:", seg, "\n")

  seg_data <- data_list[[seg]]
  f <- formulas_cb[[mname]]
  n_smooth <- count_smooth_terms(f)
  k_max <- safe_k_for(nrow(seg_data), n_smooth)
  f_safe <- if (n_smooth > 0) cap_smooth_k(f, k_max) else f

  mod <- if (nrow(seg_data) > 100) {
    bam(f_safe, data = seg_data, family = betar(link="logit"),
        method="fREML", select=TRUE, discrete=TRUE)
  } else {
    gam(f_safe, data = seg_data, family = betar(link="logit"),
        method="REML", select=TRUE)
  }
  
  diag <- check_temporal_independence(mod)
  
  df <- data.frame(Segment = seg,
                   Model = mname,
                   phi_AR1 = diag$phi_AR1,
                   DW_stat = diag$DW_stat,
                   DW_pval = diag$DW_pval,
                   LB_stat = diag$LB_stat,
                   LB_pval = diag$LB_pval)
  
  attr(df, "res_raw") <- diag$res_raw
  df
})

res_summary <- do.call(rbind, results_resid)

res_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Residual Independency Analysis - All segments"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(phi_AR1, DW_stat, DW_pval, LB_stat, LB_pval),
             decimals = 3)

pdf("acf_pacf_residuals_all.pdf")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(best_models_table))) {
  seg <- best_models_table$Segment[i]
  mname <- best_models_table$Model[i]
  res_raw <- attr(results_resid[[i]], "res_raw")
  
  par(mfrow=c(1,2))
  acf(res_raw, main=paste("ACF -", seg, mname))
  pacf(res_raw, main=paste("PACF -", seg, mname))
}
dev.off()

acf_df <- function(res, type = "ACF", site) {
  acf_obj <- acf(res, plot = FALSE)
  tibble(
    Lag = acf_obj$lag[, , 1],
    Value = acf_obj$acf[, , 1],
    Type = type,
    Site = site
  )
}

pacf_df <- function(res, type = "PACF", site) {
  pacf_obj <- pacf(res, plot = FALSE)
  tibble(
    Lag = pacf_obj$lag,
    Value = pacf_obj$acf,
    Type = type,
    Site = site
  )
}

df_all <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(best_models_table)), function(i) {
  seg <- best_models_table$Segment[i]
  res_raw <- attr(results_resid[[i]], "res_raw")
  bind_rows(
    acf_df(res_raw, "ACF", seg),
    pacf_df(res_raw, "PACF", seg)
  )
}))

custom_colors <- c(
  "Punta Maroma" = "#D55E00",
  "Florida"      = "#0072B2",
  "Saint Croix"  = "#F0E442",
  "Belize"       = "#CCBB44",
  "Regional"     = "#332288"
)

plot_acf_pacf <- ggplot(df_all, aes(x = Lag, y = Value, fill = Site)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-0.2, 0.2), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  facet_grid(Type ~ Site, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "ACF and PACF of residuals - Between sites comparisson",
       y = "Correlación", x = "Lag") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  )

plot_acf_pacf
```

### 4.6 Concurvity analysis

Concurvity diagnostics reveal marked differences in predictor redundancy across sites. At **Punta Maroma** (M4_av), concurvity for s(age) is essentially negligible (observed ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻³³), indicating near‑complete independence of age as a predictor. This underscores the robustness of the local specification, as age contributes unique explanatory power without overlap.

In **Florida** (M7_av), concurvity is high for s(age) (observed ≈ 0.92) but low for hurricane impact average (s(Hur100_av) ≈ 0.27). This suggests that while age shares explanatory variance with other predictors, hurricane effects provide independent information, reinforcing their interpretive value.

For **Belize** (M6_fqcy), concurvity values are moderate (observed ≈ 0.71–0.83), reflecting partial redundancy between age and hurricane predictors. This indicates that while the model captures relevant signals, predictor overlap may limit interpretability and requires cautious inference.

At the regional scale (M7_av), concurvity for s(age) is high (observed ≈ 0.92), consistent with strong redundancy in aggregated datasets. However, hurricane predictors retain moderate independence (estimate ≈ 0.67–0.82), supporting their inclusion in combined models to capture non‑redundant climatic signals.

**Interpretation:** These results highlight that predictor independence is strongest in **Punta Maroma**, acceptable in **Florida** for hurricane effects, and more limited in Belize and the regional dataset due to redundancy in age. The site‑specific variability in concurvity emphasizes that model validity depends on local data structure, with **Florida** and **Punta Maroma** offering the most stable predictor independence, while Belize and Regional require more cautious interpretation.

While the temporal spline (*s(age)*) is not a predictor but rather a structural term that preserves the chronology of the record, its concurvity values indicate the degree of overlap between temporal trends and climatic/disturbance predictors. At Punta Maroma, negligible concurvity confirms that the temporal trend is independent of other covariates. In Florida and the Regional panel, higher concurvity for *s(age)* reflects overlap between temporal structure and climatic signals, while hurricane predictors retain independence. In Belize, moderate concurvity suggests partial redundancy between temporal and disturbance terms. Overall, these results show that temporal structure can overlap with climatic variability, but disturbance predictors remain sufficiently independent to justify their inclusion.

**Suppl.Table 8. Concurvity diagnostics across sites.** Observed concurvity values indicate near‑independence of predictors in **Punta Maroma**, low redundancy for hurricane effects in **Florida**, moderate overlap between age and hurricane predictors in **Belize**, and high collinearity of age at the regional scale. These results highlight site‑specific variability in predictor independence, with **Florida** and **Punta Maroma** showing the most stable signals, while Belize and the regional dataset exhibit greater redundancy.

35. This code block assesses concurvity (collinearity among smooth terms) for the best GAM actually selected for each site. Previously this chunk hardcoded which terms to drop before calling `concurvity()`, and did so inconsistently with the model each site actually selected (e.g. it attempted to drop `s(Hur100_fqcy)` from Belize's model even when that model's hurricane term was `Hur100_av`, and vice versa) — a mismatch that could error out entirely. Here, `concurvity()` is instead applied directly to each site's `best_model_*` object (as fit in the previous chunk from `pars_table`/`formulas_cb`), so the smooth terms evaluated always match the model actually in use, for every site including Saint Croix.

```{r, echo=FALSE}

library(reshape2)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

concurvity_results <- lapply(best_models, function(m) concurvity(m, full = TRUE))
concurvity_results

```
